papers.title: Proportionality and Access: Divergent Standards in Administrative Sanctions and Information Rights
papers.issue: How courts balance the proportionality of administrative sanctions against the right to access information, and whether these principles operate independently or in tension.
papers.thesis: The Tetre courts apply a strict proportionality test to administrative sanctions (BD5) while maintaining a narrower, privacy-focused interpretation of access to information rights (BD1), indicating that procedural fairness in sanctioning is distinct from substantive access rights.

papers.title: Divergent Paths in Intellectual Property: Ownership and Infringement Standards
papers.issue: How do courts interpret the Tetre Intellectual Property Act regarding copyright ownership versus trademark infringement?
papers.thesis: The application of the Tetre Intellectual Property Act reveals a strict adherence to statutory definitions for copyright ownership (Section 4) and trademark infringement (Section 25), but with distinct evidentiary thresholds for each.
